keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for this regime. 'At formation, it controlled only Jiangsu, Anhui, and the north sector of Zhejiang' (the north sector is a strip the researcher drew, 118.3-122.6 E, 29.9-31.5 N; Shanghai stands inside the Reformed Government's assignment). The absorbed Provisional Government's land (Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Beijing, Tianjin) is drawn as part of the shape because the page calls it 'de jure part of this political entity', but the page also says it 'retained semi-autonomous status as the North China Political Council' and was 'under Japanese military administration'; a vassal tint may suit it better, left to the reviewer. Mengjiang is not drawn here (it has its own dossier and appears below as a vassal). Infobox area: none; the text's 'According to other sources, total extension of territory during 1940 period was 1,264,000 km2' matches this shape (about 1.27 million km2 on the grid: the Reformed Government's land about 0.35 million, the six northern units about 0.93 million), which suggests the figure counts the nominal north. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F172: the south-western corner of Shanxi is subtracted. Yan Xishan page (opened 2026-11-01): 'As the Japanese invasion pushed Yan's administration into the southwest corner of Shanxi, he established a base there where he lived in sparse conditions for eight years'; the Shanxi clique page: the invasion 'occupied most of their base province'. The corner stayed under Yan's Chongqing-aligned administration and never under the North China Political Council, so the RNG's claim there is not even nominal; the ring is the one of shanxi-clique_1938 (110.2-112.6 E, 34.6-36.6 N), cut to Shanxi so that Henan and Shaanxi are not touched. The rest of the former Provisional Government land stays nominal, as before.]

ledger.note: 30 March 1940: 'On 30 March 1940, the RNG was established in Nanjing.' 'At formation, it controlled only Jiangsu, Anhui, and the north sector of Zhejiang.' The Reformed Government page gives the same date for the merger.

region.text: Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Beijing and Tianjin, the Provisional Government's land

ledger.note: 30 March 1940: 'The RNG absorbed the Reformed Government (1938-1940) and the Provisional Government (1937-1940)'; the former Provisional Government territory 'retained semi-autonomous status as the North China Political Council'; Shandong and Hebei were 'de jure part of this political entity' but 'under Japanese military administration'. Confidence 2: the land changed hands in law only.

region.text: Mengjiang: Chahar, eastern Suiyuan and the Kalgan and Datong districts

ledger.note: 24 March 1940: 'In 1940 an agreement was signed between the Inner Mongolian puppet state of Mengjiang and the RNG, incorporating the former into the latter as an autonomous part' (RNG page); the Mengjiang page gives the date 24 March 1940. The RNG page adds that the region 'remained only nominally under RNG authority'.

region.text: Hankou and Wuchang, 'placed under control' of the government 'after 1940'

ledger.note: after 1940: 'The port of Shanghai and the cities of Hankou and Wuchang were also placed under control of the Reformed Government after 1940.' The page gives no year; 1941 is the first year after 1940 and is a placeholder. The counterpart is Japan because the Republic of China dossier records Wuhan as Japanese-occupied from October 1938.

region.text: 'Hunan, Hubei, and parts of Jiangxi provinces' (the page's words)

ledger.note: December 1941: 'During the December 1941 Japanese offensive the Reorganized Government extended its control over Hunan, Hubei, and parts of Jiangxi provinces.' One sentence, no towns; the Japanese army did not hold these provinces (the Republic of China dossier has Japan taking Changsha only in June 1944). Recorded at confidence 1 and not drawn in the keyframe; the Jiangxi strip is a guess.

9 January 1943: 'the RNG signed the Treaty on Returning Leased Territories and Repealing Extraterritoriality Rights with Japan, which abolished all foreign concessions within occupied China'; 'The RNG then took control of all of the international concessions in Shanghai and its other territories.' The page gives no separate date for the takeover. The concessions lie inside the Shanghai municipality already drawn, so no shape changes.
19 August 1945: Mengjiang is disestablished (Mengjiang page, 'disestablished 19 August 1945'); the RNG page says only that the region 'remained only nominally under RNG authority'.

union.text: Jiangsu, Anhui, Shanghai and the north of Zhejiang

ledger.note: August 1945: 'After Japan's surrender in August 1945, the RNG dissolved.' The page gives no day; the Republic of China dossier dates the formal surrender to 2 September 1945.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The regime fought no war of its own; it dissolved after Japan's surrender in August 1945.
wars.note: The war itself was not opened for this dossier; the page names no battles.

certainty.note: The page gives the core provinces; the north was nominal (North China Political Council).

The page's wider claims (Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi in December 1941; Shanghai, Hankou, Wuchang 'after 1940') are undated or vague; the keyframe draws only the core, the nominal north and the Wuhan cities.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from four pages. Not settled: (1) The page gives no capital in law (Nanjing 'still rebuilding itself'; Shanghai the 'primary focal point'). (2) The December 1941 claim (Hunan, Hubei, parts of Jiangxi) is a single sentence at odds with the Republic of China dossier's occupation events (Japan takes Changsha only in 1944); held at confidence 1 and not drawn. (3) 'Also placed under control of the Reformed Government after 1940' for Shanghai, Hankou and Wuchang gives no year; the Wuhan event is dated 1941 as a placeholder. (4) Area: the page's 'total extension of territory during 1940 period was 1,264,000 km2' (no infobox figure) agrees with the 1940 shape on the grid (about 1.27 million km2: core about 0.35 million, nominal north about 0.93 million); without the north the shape would be far below the page's figure, so the figure counts the north; the compile step may still draw the north as a vassal tint. (5) Mengjiang's zones overlap Chahar and north Shanxi inside the drawn north; Mengjiang should draw over it. (6) The Republic of China (ea-08-c) and Empire of Japan (jk-01-d) dossiers carry this land as Japanese occupation and have no event naming the Reorganized National Government; Japan's gains here are written against empire-of-japan, which should carry a matching vassal_start; a reviewer should decide. (7) The North China Political Council continued in the north to August 1945 under Japanese military administration and has no dossier. (8) Wang Jingwei: the page gives no death day. (9) Counterpart for the 1945 dissolve is republic-of-china. Family china: the colour agent may choose another.
